label: unserved rate: r144 residual/panel vs r145 row mean
why: r144's residual is a COUNT of unserved people per prompt and r145's is a rate, so the count is divided by r144's OWN persisted mean panel size -- never by a constant, because the population the numerator covers is exactly what went wrong here before. A ratio of means still differs from a mean of ratios by Jensen and 0.03 is that slack

label: unserved rate: r145 vs r146 plurality arm
why: same estimand, different inclusion floor: r146 needs a satisfaction tensor for the prompt and r145 does not

label: unserved rate: r145 vs r149 (1 - mean served)
why: r149's figure is an out-group mean within one demographic split, so it is a different population; 0.06 is generous on purpose and a gap larger than that means they are not the same quantity at all

label: South Africa plurality gap: r145 within-prompt vs r146 table
why: r146 restricts to prompts carrying a satisfaction tensor; r145 does not. Same estimator, smaller population

label: South Africa plurality gap: r145 vs r149 (unserved in minus unserved out)
why: r149 does not match on decisiveness and r145 does, so r149 should read LARGER; this checks they are the same sign and order of magnitude, not that they coincide

label: r148 internal: diff equals departure plus k times level
why: algebraic identity, but checked against the PRECISION THE FILE STORES. The first version demanded 1e-6 while the JSON rounds every value to five decimals, so three rounded numbers can differ from their own identity by up to about 1.5e-5 and the check could never pass -- the mirror of a check that cannot fail, and just as useless. A tolerance must be set by the storage precision, not by how exact the mathematics is

label: r148 vs r146: the differential under correction is the one r146 reported
why: r146's headline number must be the same differential r148 then corrected; if it is not, the retraction is aimed at a different quantity than the claim it retracts

label: veto coverage is the ASKED share, not 1.0 (R314)
why: kept at 1.0 because that is what R150's artifact still holds and the artifact is not rewritten (L81: annotate, never rewrite). It passes, and the PASS is the finding: R314 measured 5,006 of 18,678 assessments asked = 0.268. Read this row as `R150's stored coverage is still the pre-correction one`, never as `coverage is total`

label: full rejections: r150 distribution x its own n vs r151 direct count (R314)
why: the two rounds agree on the EVENT COUNT and disagree only on what to divide it by: r150 divides by all 18,562 rows it saw, r151 by the 5,006 where the question was actually posed. R314 established the second is the population and that all 195 lie inside it. Comparing the rates is a category error -- `name the estimand before the bound`

label: prompts with a full rejection: r151 vs r152
why: r152 requires a panel of at least five, so it should find at most as many; a difference above 2 prompts means the floors differ more than declared
